newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: MOTOR RACING-NANNINI TAKES DRIVE DOWN MEMORY LANE.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-NANNINI TAKES DRIVE DOWN MEMORY LANE.

text.p: Six years after he severed his arm in a helicopter crash, Italian driver Alessandro Nannini made an emotional return to Formula One on Monday.
Nannini, who was invited to drive a Benetton by his old team boss Flavio Briatore, had no hesitation in taking up the offer and he completed the special test in impressive style.

Nannini covered a total of 44 laps in the 1996 Benetton which was fitted with a special power-steering system to help his damaged right arm, which was sewn back on following the accident near his home in Siena, Italy.
"I am very happy with this first drive," he said. "Honestly, I thought it would have been more difficult after such a long break from Formula One.

"As I drove more laps, I became more and more confident and I feel that, with some set-up changes, I can improve further tomorrow. Physically, I had no problems and enjoyed the experience thoroughly."
Nannini's best lap was one minute 24.28 seconds, which compared favourably with the times set during qualifying for this year's Portuguese Grand Prix.
The time would have been good enough for fourth place on the grid for that race, most notably ahead of Benetton's leading driver Jean Alesi, who qualified with 1:24.331.
Briatore added: "Alessandro has always had a special place with the team. After the accident, I promised him that the moment he would be fit enough to drive a Formula One car, it would be a Benetton.
"I kept my promise and I am delighted that this test was a success and proof of Nannini's skill and determination."
Despite the performance, Nannini maintains that his arm will never be strong enough for him to return to Formula One.
